title: ABCD Endocarditis registry (Aachen, Bonn, Cologne, Düsseldorf)
summary: Endocarditis is a severe infection of the heart valves caused by germs. Despite modern treatment, about one in four affected people dies within one year. In this study, physicians at the university hospitals of Aachen, Bonn, Cologne, and Duesseldorf retrospectively review the medical records of patients treated for this heart valve infection between 2013 and 2024. The study examines which germs cause the infection, how it was treated, how the disease has changed over the years – for example in people with artificial heart valves – and which circumstances are linked to a more severe course. The aim is to identify patients at risk earlier and to improve treatment. No additional examinations are required; only existing medical records are analysed, without disclosing any names.

interventions.name: Single-arm observational cohort without intervention: all patients (≥ 18 years) with infective endocarditis treated as inpatients at one of the four participating university hospitals (Aachen, Bonn, Cologne, Duesseldorf) between 1 January 2013 and 31 December 2024. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inpatient treatment for infective endocarditis at one of the four participating university hospitals (Aachen, Bonn, Cologne, Duesseldorf) between 1 January 2013 and 31 December 2024; identification via ICD-10-GM codes I33, I38, I39, A39.51, A52.03, and B37.6; confirmation of definite or possible infective endocarditis according to the Duke criteria upon review of the medical records.
Exclusion criteria:
Age below 18 years; exclusion of the diagnosis of infective endocarditis according to the Duke criteria upon chart review; absence of evaluable medical records. In patients with more than one endocarditis episode, only the first episode is analysed.
